title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for heart rhythm management.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old woman presenting for a routine follow-up of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. She reports that her symptoms have been well-managed with her current regimen. She occasionally experiences palpitations but denies any syncope, chest pain, or significant shortness of breath. She remains compliant with her rate-control medications and her anticoagulant therapy.

Medication List
Apixaban 5 mg twice daily
Metoprolol 25 mg daily

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress and is alert and oriented. Heart rate is 72 beats per minute, regular rhythm. Blood pressure is 128/82 mmHg. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No peripheral edema noted.

Assessment
1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The patient is currently stable on rate control and continues to take apixaban for prevention of thromboembolic events.

Plan
Continue current medications as prescribed. The patient will continue to monitor for any new symptoms and follow up in three months.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026

distractors.why: The provider documents paroxysmal, not permanent.
Apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin and similar drugs are anticoagulants (Z79.01).
